summary: New head coach Marco Rose has a lot to live up after last season’s sixth-placed finish while fans have a first year in Europe to look forward to
content: Guardian writers’ predicted position: 12th (NB: this is not necessarily Ben Fisher’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips) Last season’s position: 6th Prospects It was the day after the final game of last season at Bournemouth’s secluded, swish training base and, before clearing his belongings on his last day in the building, the departing head coach, Andoni Iraola, spent a couple of hours in his office chewing the fat with his successor, Marco Rose, talking players, pubs and tactics. The story goes that, with time moving on, Tiago Pinto, the club’s sporting director, knocked on the door to advise them there were other things to tackle. It was an interesting scenario that speaks volumes of the respect between the pair. Long before joining Bournemouth, Iraola cited Rose’s Borussia Mönchengladbach side as one of his favourite teams to watch, the German’s “vertical football” helping them qualify for the Champions League in Rose’s first season in charge. Rose accepts that Iraola, in absorbing the sales of key players totalling more than £250m last season and qualifying for Europe for the first time, has set a high bar. Remarkably, Bournemouth did not lose a game after the sale of Antoine Semenyo in the second week of January. Rose put it succinctly during pre-season in Austria. “Andoni didn’t leave a lot of space to improve,” he said. “Pressure’s on.” In his first session, Rose told the players he loved the way they attacked the Premier League last season. Playing in the Europa League, however, represents uncharted territory for a team in the second tier as recently as four years ago. It is why Bournemouth’s hierarchy contacted peers at Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest to understand the realities of juggling the Thursday-Sunday rhythm the competition will bring. Rose is close friends with Oliver Glasner, who is now at Forest, but won the Conference League last season with Palace. “We are not going to Europe just to enjoy, we want to be competitive,” Rose said. “We are not there just to watch.” Unlike last summer, so far they have retained all key players, chiefly Alex Scott, Rayan and Eli Junior Kroupi, the 20-year-old forward who breezed into double figures in his debut Premier League season and the club consider a generational talent. Kroupi attracted serious interest from Paris Saint-Germain, among other European superpowers, but a freak foot injury during a pre-season drill means he is sidelined for at least three months. At the end of the season, Bournemouth earmarked a centre-back to replace Marcos Senesi and a striker to compete with Evanilson as key priorities and by the start of August the club had recruited Álvaro Rodríguez, whom Rose wanted to sign at Leipzig, and António Silva from Elche and Benfica respectively. Juanlu Sánchez joined from Sevilla to provide competition for Adam Smith, the evergreen 35-year-old into his 14th season at the club, and will also fill the void left by Álex Jiménez, who has joined Fiorentina on loan with an option to sign permanently because he remains suspended in England while under investigation by the Football Association. Off-field picture The smallest stadium in the Premier League has been a building site this summer, with the club working to ensure their 11,357-seater ground complies with Uefa regulations. There has been a wider facelift, too, with every seat being replaced, while they are filling in two corners to increase the capacity by 800 this season. Playing in Europe brings the challenge of meeting Uefa’s squad-cost ratio (SCR) rules, which caps on-pitch spending at 70% of a club’s revenue. Bournemouth finished the 2025-26 season at 82% and they continue to work towards meeting the threshold. Last month the academy was awarded category one status, four years after being category three. Owner-fan relationship The American billionaire Bill Foley described himself as a dictator upon buying the club approaching four years ago, but supporters are grateful for his naked ambition. Foley, who made his fortune in insurance, is forthright and somewhat prophetic. In 2023, he said the club would play in Europe within five years – and achieved it in three. It was a similar story with Vegas Golden Knights, whom he vowed would win the Stanley Cup within six years of him launching the ice hockey franchise in 2017 – they won it in their sixth season. Foley recently added rugby union’s Exeter Chiefs to his sporting stable, which extends to Lorient, Auckland FC and Moreirense. Not every decision is universally popular but Foley, who turns 82 in December and predominantly splits his time between California and Vegas, puts his money where his mouth is. The manager As a defender, Marco Rose was schooled by Jürgen Klopp and Thomas Tuchel at Mainz, and Ralf Rangnick at Hannover, so had quite the education before beginning his coaching career at home town club Lokomotive Leipzig. Klopp told Rose, after promotion to the Bundesliga in 2004, that he would excel in the dugout and he has since managed some of the biggest names: Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham at Borussia Dortmund, Dominik Szoboszlai and Dani Olmo at RB Leipzig. Rose has been compared to Klopp and, naturally, Iraola, given his appetite for high-energy tactics. Bournemouth routed Genoa 10-1 in pre-season so, could his style be even more aggressive than Iraola’s? “I would say [to be] even more aggressive than Andoni is quite difficult,” came the reply. His grandfather, Walter Rose, represented Germany in 1937. Star signing These days, £50m is about the going rate for an elite defender. Tottenham paid £52m to sign Jan Paul van Hecke. Chelsea paid the same fee to take Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace. Bournemouth pocketed £50m when Dean Huijsen joined Real Madrid last year, though that price was set by a release clause. chineseTitle: 英超联赛 2026-27 预览第 3 名：伯恩茅斯
chineseSummary: 新任主教练马可·罗斯在上赛季获得第六名后有很多事情要做，而球迷们也对欧洲的第一年充满期待
chineseContent: 《卫报》撰稿人的预测排名：第 12 位（注意：这不一定是本·费舍尔的预测，而是我们撰稿人提示的平均值） 上赛季排名：第 6 位 前景 那是上赛季最后一场比赛后的第二天，在伯恩茅斯僻静而豪华的训练基地，在他在大楼的最后一天清理自己的物品之前，即将离任的主教练安多尼·伊拉奥拉在他的办公室里和他的继任者一起嚼了几个小时的脂肪，马可·罗斯，会说话的球员，酒吧和战术。故事是这样的，随着时间的推移，俱乐部的体育总监蒂亚戈·平托敲门告诉他们还有其他事情需要解决。这是一个有趣的场景，充分说明了两人之间的尊重。早在加盟伯恩茅斯之前，伊劳拉就将罗斯的门兴格拉德巴赫队视为他最喜欢观看的球队之一，德国人的“垂直足球”帮助他们在罗斯执教的第一个赛季获得了欧冠资格。罗斯承认，伊劳拉上赛季吸收了主力球员总销售额超过 2.5 亿英镑并首次获得欧洲资格，树立了很高的标准。值得注意的是，在一月第二周出售安托万·塞梅尼奥后，伯恩茅斯没有输掉一场比赛。罗斯在奥地利季前赛期间简洁地说道。 “安多尼没有留下太多改进的空间，”他说。 “压力来了。”在他的第一堂课中，罗斯告诉球员们他喜欢他们上赛季进攻英超的方式。然而，就在四年前，参加欧罗巴联赛对于第二级别的球队来说还是一个未知的领域。这就是为什么伯恩茅斯的高层联系了水晶宫和诺丁汉森林的同行，以了解如何平衡周四至周日的节奏，比赛将带来怎样的现实。
